This is EQU's block. Outside-route roles for EQU (weighted): IO outside routes 19,850; register/head choice outside 17,926; stack switch outside 5,546; control 3,621; label read 2,101 (probably outside?); etc. Outside-route total for EQU ≈ 19,850+17,926+5,546+3,621+2,101+493+478+28 ≈ 50,043. Extra IO reads 19,850 = ~40% — still not "most". So "Most of these are extra reads" is unsupported for both NOT (28%) and EQU (40%). Objection confirmed: the largest single kind but not most. Fix: "The largest single kind of these is extra reads" or "Many of these are extra reads".

Hmm wait — for plain words: "About one in six of them is not on the path from the numbers to the answer at all. Most of these are extra reads". Note also plain words says these off-path ones are "extra reads" whose removal "shifts every later read by one". The md says the 17% are "the IO reads that set the rotation, stack switches, control instructions and register choices of instructions outside the route". So md itself lists several kinds without saying IO is most. Plain words says "Most of these are extra reads" — not in md, contradicted by json. Good.

Now, other checks:

- "every pair of instructions in every program that copies itself and does a sum (52 million runs)" — md: "every pair of sites whose single ablation leaves replication was ablated in every replicating sequence that performs a task". Plain words overstates: not every pair, only pairs whose single ablation leaves replication. Fix: "every pair that could be tried without stopping the copying first".

- §1 "In the other 2 in 100, a second copy of the sum inside the same program meant two instructions had to go together." — leaves out the 89 unstopped and 2 triples; §3 covers them. Since §1 is the direct answer, misdescribing the residual 2% is a real objection (medium). Also "a second copy... one from each place" for pairs: md says "or of the rotation and one route" — so not always one from each place.

- "whose only job is to make sure the right number arrives at the right moment" (§1) — "only job" too strong given results mark the role of off-path sites as read-from-trace, tested by removal in three cases only (md §7 Unsure). Minor objection: soften to "whose job, as far as Avida's own records show, is...". Actually, "make sure the right number arrives at the right moment" — the mechanism is that removing it shifts the rotation. Their role is setting which number later reads get — md states that as read from trace. Hmm, the md states it confidently too ("extra IO reads that are not on the path at all but set which input number the later reads receive"). The "unsure" is about the role of a required site outside the route "read from what it was executed as, not tested one by one (three reruns only)". So the role assignment is flagged unsure in the results; plain words §1 states it flatly, though §6 flags it. Borderline — I'll fold it into a minor objection or mention alongside.

- §3 line 40: "the read-and-hand-out instruction (a quarter to two fifths of them)" — IO share ranges 24%–40% by kind table. 24% is slightly below a quarter. Very minor; "a quarter to two fifths" vs 24–40%. I'll skip or mention as trivial. Probably skip — rounding "about a quarter". Actually the requirement is "no rounding that changes a comparison" — 24% → "a quarter" changes nothing material. Skip.

- "five kinds of step" — check against example: steps named in the EQU example: nand, addition, "add one", subtraction (4 kinds of combining) + reads/hand-out + pile. Md §0: "a few nand steps, sometimes with add, sub, inc, dec steps". "Five kinds" isn't in the results; and in the example given there are four arithmetic kinds. If "five kinds" means nand+add+inc+sub+IO... unclear. Minor objection: change to "a few kinds of step" or say "nand and at most four kinds of arithmetic". I'll include as minor.

- §2: "Avida has one instruction that combines numbers: it is called nand" — "combines numbers" also loosely covers add/sub/inc/dec mentioned next sentence ("Avida also has instructions that add..."). Fine.

- §2 line 23: "An instruction such as 'combine' acts on the storage places; a small marker instruction placed right after it can say which storage place it uses." ✓ matches nop behavior.

- §2 line 21: "the simulated computer hands a program numbers, and the program earns a reward if it hands back certain combinations of them" — ✓.

- "nothing that copies itself ran on a real one" ✓ style consistent with 111.

- Check §3 line 33: "instruction 12 puts it on a pile" — push ✓. "instruction 16 takes it off into the second storage place" — pop into CX; "second storage place" ambiguous as discussed; skip.

- Check "about 5 for the simplest sum (NOT)" — NAND is equally ~5 but simplest is NOT (1 step) — fine.

- §4 line 61: "each run's program ancestry (its line of parent and descendant programs) found its own" — md says "each run's program ancestry settled on its own circuits" for the most common circuits of AND, OR, NOR, XOR, EQU confined to one to seven runs. Matches md. OK.

- §4 line 63: "'not both A and C, plus A, plus one' is always 'A and not C'" — md gives nand(x,y)+x+1 = x and not y ✓.

- §4 line 63 "Checked on all eight combinations of three digits, every circuit that could be checked this way gives its sum, except one." ✓.

- §5: "Make it mean and: almost all sums vanish except AND (73 in 100 remain) and some NOT and ANDN." — table: NOT 18%, NAND 1%, AND 73%, ANDN 20%, rest 0. ✓.

- §5 "Numbers of the kind Avida hands out in its runs: 99 to 100 in 100 still do each sum." ✓.

- §5 "Change all the meanings... no program copies itself or does anything." ✓ md. But note "the 26 letters the 26 meanings in another order" — shufflings keep 3 nop meanings among a–c and shuffle 23, and 2–4 letters keep meaning by chance. §6 says markers kept in front but not the chance-retention.
